title: Warm up, then decay along a cosine
brief: Build linear warmup, the cosine decay fraction, and the full schedule, then run Adam with it on noisy mini-batches.
hints: linear_warmup(step, warmup, peak) is peak * step / warmup while step < warmup and peak after that. Check warmup <= 0 before you divide.
cosine_decay_fraction(p) clamps p to [0, 1], then returns 0.5 * (1 + cos(pi * p)). It is 1 at p = 0, 0.5 at p = 0.5, and 0 at p = 1.
In cosine_schedule, p is measured from the end of warmup: (step - warmup) / (total - warmup). Compute it only after you have handled warmup >= total.
The four anchor points are 0 at step 0, the peak at the end of warmup, half the peak halfway through the decay, and 0 at the last step.
